newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-German industry orders rise for 3rd month.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German industry orders rise for 3rd month.

text.p: Industrial orders in Germany rose 0.6 percent in August from July, the third consecutive monthly rise, but slowed slightly from a 0.9 percent increase in July, the economics ministry said.
Orders were up 4.4 percent from the year-earlier level, jumping from a 0.5 percent increase in July, according to Bundesbank data.
The rise slightly exceeded market expectations and suggests "the German recovery remains in fine fettle," economist Robert Prior-Wandesforde at James Capel said.
"The evidence from the orders data, however, suggests that the bulk of demand may now be coming from abroad," he added.
Domestic orders were down 1.0 percent frome the previous month, while foreign orders rose 3.0 percent.

Trinkaus Capital Management in Duesseldorf said the latest industrial orders and production data, together with the Ifo business climate index, paint a picture of a moderate and slightly weakening recovery.
"Overall, this should allow the favourable domestic bond-market environment to hold for the mid-term," Trinkaus said in a faxed comment on the data.
In west Germany, orders rose 0.6 percent from July and 4.8 percent from the year-earlier month, while in east Germany they fell 3.6 and 4.9 percent, respectively.
